decisions.reason: As a recently launched multi-model extension of the core drainage range, it likely stays because the firm has already committed development and portfolio space to it, even though the lighter website emphasis makes exit somewhat easier than for flagship launches.

This product fits the firm's stated direction toward modern bathroom architecture, was given its own page, and is close to the established offer, so management would be inclined to continue rather than admit an early reversal.

A pump-assisted line likely required meaningful engineering effort and broadens the firm's drainage solution set, so under escalation of commitment management would tend to keep it and explain any early weakness as temporary market adoption effects.
Because it is a close-to-core drain product with its own page and clear relevance to barrier-free, design-oriented bathrooms, the firm is likely to maintain it rather than write off a fresh launch.

Although this grate is a narrower design-focused addition, the public presentation on its own page and the firm's broad-range strategy make continued support more likely than withdrawal after only about a year.
